title: Assembly of prime power summands
statement: For a property P of lifted-integer modules that contains zero objects, is invariant under isomorphism, and is closed under short exact extensions, let M be a finite module annihilated by a nonzero natural number n. If P holds for every lifted ZMod (r ^ e) whenever r is prime, r divides n, and multiplication by r on M is not injective, then P M.

proof.text: Use AddCommGroup.equiv_directSum_zmod_of_finite on M, then DirectSum.addEquivProd and coordinatewise ULift to get an additive equivalence from M to a finite product of lifted ZMod(p_i^e_i). Every additive equivalence between lifted-integer modules is linear: each lifted integer is the integer cast of its down value, and map_intCast_smul supplies compatibility. This gives the module isomorphism used for transport.

For each index with e_i=0, the cyclic module is zero and hzero applies. For e_i nonzero, compose the direct-sum injection with the inverse decomposition to obtain an injective additive homomorphism g:ZMod(p_i^e_i) -> M. Apply hM to g(1) and use injectivity and map_nsmul to obtain (n:ZMod(p_i^e_i))=0. ZMod.natCast_eq_zero_iff gives p_i^e_i dividing n; since e_i is nonzero, p_i divides n.

If multiplication by p_i on M were injective, induction on the exponent using mul_nsmul would make multiplication by p_i^e_i injective. But p_i^e_i kills g(1), so g(1)=0 and injectivity of g gives 1=0 in ZMod(p_i^e_i). The same cast-divisibility criterion would give p_i^e_i dividing 1, contradicting 1<p_i^e_i. Thus hp applies to every nontrivial factor.

Prove extension-closed properties are closed under finite products by Fintype.induction_empty_option. The empty product is zero; reindexing is transported by LinearEquiv.piCongrLeft; adjoining one factor is transported by LinearEquiv.piOptionEquivProd from a binary product. The binary product is a biproduct via ModuleCat.biprodIsoProd, and ShortComplex.Splitting.ofHasBinaryBiproduct.shortExact supplies its split short exact sequence. Apply hext and finally transport along the inverse module isomorphism from the first step.

proof_origin.place: cyclic-coefficient reduction; equiv_directSum_zmod_of_finite; Splitting.ofHasBinaryBiproduct; explicit finite-product assembly

lean.statement: theorem finite_torsion_assemble_prime_powers (P : ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ) → Prop) (hzero : ∀ A, IsZero A → P A) (hiso : ∀ {A B}, (A ≅ B) → P A → P B) (hext : ∀ (S : ShortComplex (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ))), S.ShortExact → P S.X₁ → P S.X₃ → P S.X₂) (M : ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ)) [Finite M] (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≠ 0) (hM : ∀ x : M, n • x = 0) (hp : ∀ r e : ℕ, r.Prime → r ∣ n → ¬ Function.Injective (fun x : M ↦ r • x) → P (ModuleCat.of (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ) (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod (r ^ e))))) : P M
